title: WPMS/599/2024 of SATYA PAL SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 599 of 2024
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

(1) Mr. D.P. Mittal, learned counsel for
the petitioner.
(2) Mr. K.K. Shah, learned Additional
C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
(3) Petitioner is a borrower, who is
facing recovery proceedings. I n this writ
petition, petitioner has sought the
following relief: -
(i) I ssue a writ order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus to directing the
respondents to give time to pay the
amount mentioned in the impugned order
dated 28.07.2023 issued by the
respondent no. 1, whereby the petitioner
has been directed to pay a sum of Rs.
18,06,380.65/ - only (Rupees Eighteen
Lakhs Six thousand and three hundred
eighty & sixty five paisa).
(ii) I ssue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondents not to take any coercive
measure against the petitioner with
respect to the impugned order dated
28.07.2023 and alternatively to accept the
aforesaid loan amount in equal and easy
instalments as will be fixed by this Hon'ble
court in the facts and circumstances of the
present case.
(4) Learned counsel for petitioner
submits that a settlem ent was arrived at
between petitioner and respondent no.
2, according to which, petitioner had to
pay ₹17.00 lakh to respondent no. 2. He

further submits that due to financial
incapacity, it is not possible to petitioner
to deposit the said am ount in one go,
therefore, he m ay be permitted to repay
the amount of one tim e settlem ent, in
instalm ents.
(5) The relief, as claimed in the writ
petition, cannot be granted. Firstly, such
lending organisation is a private body,
which is not 'State' under Article 12 of
the Constitution. Secondly, a settlement
arrived at between parties cannot be
tinkered with Constitutional Court,
m erely on the ground of financial
incapacity of the petitioner. I f petitioner
had any grievance qua the settlement
arrived at between him and respondent
no. 2, it is open to him to approach
respondent no. 2, highlighting his
difficulties. Thus, there is no scope for
interference in the present case.
(6) Accordingly, writ petition fails and is
dismissed. No order as to costs.
( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 11.03.2024
